hints.title: Use one shared count
hints.body: All urns have the same positive integer number n of balls. Evaluate every label at that one n.
hints.pitfall: Do not choose a different ball count for each urn.
hints.pause: List the truth values for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>4</mn></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Count whole true statements only after evaluating them at the same allowed input.

hints.title: Notice equivalent labels
hints.body: S says one or two balls; T says fewer than three. On the positive-integer domain these are equivalent, so they are either both true or both false.
hints.recap: Equivalent labels cannot contain the sole truth.
hints.pitfall: The positivity assumption is needed for that equivalence.
hints.pause: Which n-values can be excluded because S and T would both hold?

recall.reminder: Equivalent statements have the same truth value and cannot be the only true statement separately.

hints.title: Finish the shared truth table
hints.body: For every count not yet excluded, evaluate each urn label at that same count. Treat all counts above four as one case.
hints.recap: Exactly one true label is a condition on the entire row.
hints.pitfall: Zero true labels also fails the condition.
hints.pause: Finish the rows and identify any row with exactly one truth.

recall.reminder: Exactly one true label is a condition on the entire row.

solution:
Let the common positive integer count be n. At n=1, P, S, T are true. At n=2, Q, S, T are true. At n=3, only R is true. At n=4, P, Q, R are true. For n≥5, no label is true.

These cases cover every allowed count, so exactly one true label is possible only at n=3, where the truthful label belongs to urn R.

Answer C: urn R.
knowledgePattern: Exhaust a common integer parameter under exactly-one truth
